title: Close-Out Price of a Discontinued Item: Contract Pricing Agreement Contract Administration
content:
# Close-out price of a discontinued item — contract administration note (Contract Pricing Agreement)

**Item in view.** The item of the latest backorder on the customer's ship-tos, as the customer's Ship-To Fulfillment Account records show it, when the agreement carries an added price line for that item, that backorder was filled with a Corbett-approved substitute of another item number, and the agreement carries no removal line for the item yet. The discontinuation date is the ship date of that substitute fill. Calendar days from one date to another count the later date and not the earlier one. Wherever a latest or most recent record of a kind is taken, it is the one with the latest date, and among records of the same date the one recorded first.

**Close-out price.** The close-out price is the contract unit price on the discontinued item's latest price line; it is rounded half up to four decimal places once, on the final figure. The concessions set for the close-out are added together and taken off the close-out price once, before that rounding.

| Check on the records | Needed for the item to be in view |
|---|---|
| Latest backorder on any of the customer's ship-tos | Its item is the item in view |
| Added price line for that item on the agreement | Present |
| Fill of that backorder | With a different item number (the substitute) |
| Removal line for the item on the agreement | Absent |

**Worked example (hypothetical).** An item whose latest price line carries a contract unit price of 14.2500, its backorder filled with a substitute shipped on a given date: the close-out line is effective on that ship date at 14.2500.
